scope: Source check for package-boundary and OPFS/storage posture work; used to avoid adding doctrine detached from browser-platform constraints.

sources.finding: OPFS is origin-private browser storage that remains quota-bound, needs no file permission prompt, and is removed when site storage is cleared.
Web Locks AbortSignal rejects queued requests before grant; once a lock has been granted the signal is ignored, so provider/lifecycle cancellation must remain explicit.
Web Locks coordinate same-origin asynchronous work but are not a durability, quota, or fairness guarantee.
Storage Buckets are available in Chromium-family capability space and can make eviction policy more predictable, but this is not a cross-browser baseline.
Bucket quota and durability controls are policy inputs/hints that should be observed as capabilities, not assumed as fsync or crash guarantees.
Storage quota and eviction criteria vary by browser and user-agent policy, reinforcing BrowserRT quota/eviction non-claims.
Recent public reporting on FROST treats OPFS-backed SSD timing as a browser privacy side channel, so high-volume OPFS IO should be treated as a byte-time/privacy surface.

appliedToThisTurn: Prioritized package boundary relief over a new registry because browser-local mutation needs a small install surface before more proof layers.
Kept OPFS/Web Locks/Storage Buckets/fingerprintability as non-claims and future guards rather than implying current browser durability or privacy coverage.
Ratchet examples after reducing bytes so the cube cannot silently drift back to the near-failing package example boundary.
speculation: The next product-risk failure is likely package src pressure, not package examples, because published source remains within roughly 1.4 KB of its ratchet.

Heavy proof/demo helpers are probably inside the published runtime boundary because examples needed evidence witnesses; a cleaner split should keep adoption APIs published while moving support/evidence helpers out of the default package.

Any future high-IO OPFS local-first demo should carry a byte-time/privacy budget before it claims user value, otherwise it can optimize toward behavior that modern browser research treats as fingerprintable.
nonClaims: This source check is not a compatibility matrix, browser test run, security review, Storage Buckets implementation, privacy guarantee, or proof of OPFS durability.
